8341namespace nlohmann
8342{
8343namespace detail
8344{
8346// binary writer //
8348
8352template<typename BasicJsonType, typename CharType>
8353class binary_writer
8354{
8355 using string_t = typename BasicJsonType::string_t;
8356
8357 public:
8363 explicit binary_writer(output_adapter_t<CharType> adapter) : oa(adapter)
8364 {
8365 assert(oa);
8366 }
8367
8372 void write_bson(const BasicJsonType& j)
8373 {
8374 switch (j.type())
8375 {
8376 case value_t::object:
8377 {
8378 write_bson_object(*j.m_value.object);
8379 break;
8380 }
8381
8382 default:
8383 {
8384 JSON_THROW(type_error::create(317, "to serialize to BSON, top-level type must be object, but is " + std::string(j.type_name())));
8385 }
8386 }
8387 }
8388
8392 void write_cbor(const BasicJsonType& j)
8393 {
8394 switch (j.type())
8395 {
8396 case value_t::null:
8397 {
8398 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xF6));
8399 break;
8400 }
8401
8402 case value_t::boolean:
8403 {
8404 oa->write_character(j.m_value.boolean
8405 ? to_char_type(0xF5)
8406 : to_char_type(0xF4));
8407 break;
8408 }
8409
8410 case value_t::number_integer:
8411 {
8412 if (j.m_value.number_integer >= 0)
8413 {
8414 // CBOR does not differentiate between positive signed
8415 // integers and unsigned integers. Therefore, we used the
8416 // code from the value_t::number_unsigned case here.
8417 if (j.m_value.number_integer <= 0x17)
8418 {
8419 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8420 }
8421 else if (j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8422 {
8423 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x18));
8424 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8425 }
8426 else if (j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8427 {
8428 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x19));
8429 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8430 }
8431 else if (j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8432 {
8433 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x1A));
8434 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8435 }
8436 else
8437 {
8438 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x1B));
8439 write_number(static_cast<uint64_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8440 }
8441 }
8442 else
8443 {
8444 // The conversions below encode the sign in the first
8445 // byte, and the value is converted to a positive number.
8446 const auto positive_number = -1 - j.m_value.number_integer;
8447 if (j.m_value.number_integer >= -24)
8448 {
8449 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(0x20 + positive_number));
8450 }
8451 else if (positive_number <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8452 {
8453 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x38));
8454 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(positive_number));
8455 }
8456 else if (positive_number <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8457 {
8458 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x39));
8459 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(positive_number));
8460 }
8461 else if (positive_number <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8462 {
8463 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x3A));
8464 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(positive_number));
8465 }
8466 else
8467 {
8468 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x3B));
8469 write_number(static_cast<uint64_t>(positive_number));
8470 }
8471 }
8472 break;
8473 }
8474
8475 case value_t::number_unsigned:
8476 {
8477 if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= 0x17)
8478 {
8479 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(j.m_value.number_unsigned));
8480 }
8481 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8482 {
8483 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x18));
8484 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(j.m_value.number_unsigned));
8485 }
8486 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8487 {
8488 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x19));
8489 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(j.m_value.number_unsigned));
8490 }
8491 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8492 {
8493 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x1A));
8494 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(j.m_value.number_unsigned));
8495 }
8496 else
8497 {
8498 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x1B));
8499 write_number(static_cast<uint64_t>(j.m_value.number_unsigned));
8500 }
8501 break;
8502 }
8503
8504 case value_t::number_float:
8505 {
8506 oa->write_character(get_cbor_float_prefix(j.m_value.number_float));
8507 write_number(j.m_value.number_float);
8508 break;
8509 }
8510
8511 case value_t::string:
8512 {
8513 // step 1: write control byte and the string length
8514 const auto N = j.m_value.string->size();
8515 if (N <= 0x17)
8516 {
8517 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(0x60 + N));
8518 }
8519 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8520 {
8521 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x78));
8522 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(N));
8523 }
8524 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8525 {
8526 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x79));
8527 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(N));
8528 }
8529 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8530 {
8531 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x7A));
8532 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(N));
8533 }
8534 // LCOV_EXCL_START
8535 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max)())
8536 {
8537 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x7B));
8538 write_number(static_cast<uint64_t>(N));
8539 }
8540 // LCOV_EXCL_STOP
8541
8542 // step 2: write the string
8543 oa->write_characters(
8544 reinterpret_cast<const CharType*>(j.m_value.string->c_str()),
8545 j.m_value.string->size());
8546 break;
8547 }
8548
8549 case value_t::array:
8550 {
8551 // step 1: write control byte and the array size
8552 const auto N = j.m_value.array->size();
8553 if (N <= 0x17)
8554 {
8555 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(0x80 + N));
8556 }
8557 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8558 {
8559 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x98));
8560 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(N));
8561 }
8562 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8563 {
8564 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x99));
8565 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(N));
8566 }
8567 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8568 {
8569 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x9A));
8570 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(N));
8571 }
8572 // LCOV_EXCL_START
8573 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max)())
8574 {
8575 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x9B));
8576 write_number(static_cast<uint64_t>(N));
8577 }
8578 // LCOV_EXCL_STOP
8579
8580 // step 2: write each element
8581 for (const auto& el : *j.m_value.array)
8582 {
8583 write_cbor(el);
8584 }
8585 break;
8586 }
8587
8588 case value_t::object:
8589 {
8590 // step 1: write control byte and the object size
8591 const auto N = j.m_value.object->size();
8592 if (N <= 0x17)
8593 {
8594 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(0xA0 + N));
8595 }
8596 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8597 {
8598 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xB8));
8599 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(N));
8600 }
8601 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8602 {
8603 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xB9));
8604 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(N));
8605 }
8606 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8607 {
8608 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xBA));
8609 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(N));
8610 }
8611 // LCOV_EXCL_START
8612 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max)())
8613 {
8614 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xBB));
8615 write_number(static_cast<uint64_t>(N));
8616 }
8617 // LCOV_EXCL_STOP
8618
8619 // step 2: write each element
8620 for (const auto& el : *j.m_value.object)
8621 {
8622 write_cbor(el.first);
8623 write_cbor(el.second);
8624 }
8625 break;
8626 }
8627
8628 default:
8629 break;
8630 }
8631 }
8632
8636 void write_msgpack(const BasicJsonType& j)
8637 {
8638 switch (j.type())
8639 {
8640 case value_t::null: // nil
8641 {
8642 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xC0));
8643 break;
8644 }
8645
8646 case value_t::boolean: // true and false
8647 {
8648 oa->write_character(j.m_value.boolean
8649 ? to_char_type(0xC3)
8650 : to_char_type(0xC2));
8651 break;
8652 }
8653
8654 case value_t::number_integer:
8655 {
8656 if (j.m_value.number_integer >= 0)
8657 {
8658 // MessagePack does not differentiate between positive
8659 // signed integers and unsigned integers. Therefore, we used
8660 // the code from the value_t::number_unsigned case here.
8661 if (j.m_value.number_unsigned < 128)
8662 {
8663 // positive fixnum
8664 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8665 }
8666 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8667 {
8668 // uint 8
8669 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xCC));
8670 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8671 }
8672 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8673 {
8674 // uint 16
8675 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xCD));
8676 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8677 }
8678 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8679 {
8680 // uint 32
8681 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xCE));
8682 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8683 }
8684 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max)())
8685 {
8686 // uint 64
8687 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xCF));
8688 write_number(static_cast<uint64_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8689 }
8690 }
8691 else
8692 {
8693 if (j.m_value.number_integer >= -32)
8694 {
8695 // negative fixnum
8696 write_number(static_cast<int8_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8697 }
8698 else if (j.m_value.number_integer >= (std::numeric_limits<int8_t>::min)() and
8699 j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<int8_t>::max)())
8700 {
8701 // int 8
8702 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xD0));
8703 write_number(static_cast<int8_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8704 }
8705 else if (j.m_value.number_integer >= (std::numeric_limits<int16_t>::min)() and
8706 j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<int16_t>::max)())
8707 {
8708 // int 16
8709 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xD1));
8710 write_number(static_cast<int16_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8711 }
8712 else if (j.m_value.number_integer >= (std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::min)() and
8713 j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max)())
8714 {
8715 // int 32
8716 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xD2));
8717 write_number(static_cast<int32_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8718 }
8719 else if (j.m_value.number_integer >= (std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::min)() and
8720 j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max)())
8721 {
8722 // int 64
8723 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xD3));
8724 write_number(static_cast<int64_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8725 }
8726 }
8727 break;
8728 }
8729
8730 case value_t::number_unsigned:
8731 {
8732 if (j.m_value.number_unsigned < 128)
8733 {
8734 // positive fixnum
8735 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8736 }
8737 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8738 {
8739 // uint 8
8740 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xCC));
8741 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8742 }
8743 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8744 {
8745 // uint 16
8746 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xCD));
8747 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8748 }
8749 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8750 {
8751 // uint 32
8752 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xCE));
8753 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8754 }
8755 else if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max)())
8756 {
8757 // uint 64
8758 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xCF));
8759 write_number(static_cast<uint64_t>(j.m_value.number_integer));
8760 }
8761 break;
8762 }
8763
8764 case value_t::number_float:
8765 {
8766 oa->write_character(get_msgpack_float_prefix(j.m_value.number_float));
8767 write_number(j.m_value.number_float);
8768 break;
8769 }
8770
8771 case value_t::string:
8772 {
8773 // step 1: write control byte and the string length
8774 const auto N = j.m_value.string->size();
8775 if (N <= 31)
8776 {
8777 // fixstr
8778 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(0xA0 | N));
8779 }
8780 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
8781 {
8782 // str 8
8783 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xD9));
8784 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(N));
8785 }
8786 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8787 {
8788 // str 16
8789 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xDA));
8790 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(N));
8791 }
8792 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8793 {
8794 // str 32
8795 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xDB));
8796 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(N));
8797 }
8798
8799 // step 2: write the string
8800 oa->write_characters(
8801 reinterpret_cast<const CharType*>(j.m_value.string->c_str()),
8802 j.m_value.string->size());
8803 break;
8804 }
8805
8806 case value_t::array:
8807 {
8808 // step 1: write control byte and the array size
8809 const auto N = j.m_value.array->size();
8810 if (N <= 15)
8811 {
8812 // fixarray
8813 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(0x90 | N));
8814 }
8815 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8816 {
8817 // array 16
8818 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xDC));
8819 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(N));
8820 }
8821 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8822 {
8823 // array 32
8824 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xDD));
8825 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(N));
8826 }
8827
8828 // step 2: write each element
8829 for (const auto& el : *j.m_value.array)
8830 {
8831 write_msgpack(el);
8832 }
8833 break;
8834 }
8835
8836 case value_t::object:
8837 {
8838 // step 1: write control byte and the object size
8839 const auto N = j.m_value.object->size();
8840 if (N <= 15)
8841 {
8842 // fixmap
8843 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(0x80 | (N & 0xF)));
8844 }
8845 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint16_t>::max)())
8846 {
8847 // map 16
8848 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xDE));
8849 write_number(static_cast<uint16_t>(N));
8850 }
8851 else if (N <= (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max)())
8852 {
8853 // map 32
8854 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0xDF));
8855 write_number(static_cast<uint32_t>(N));
8856 }
8857
8858 // step 2: write each element
8859 for (const auto& el : *j.m_value.object)
8860 {
8861 write_msgpack(el.first);
8862 write_msgpack(el.second);
8863 }
8864 break;
8865 }
8866
8867 default:
8868 break;
8869 }
8870 }
8871
8878 void write_ubjson(const BasicJsonType& j, const bool use_count,
8879 const bool use_type, const bool add_prefix = true)
8880 {
8881 switch (j.type())
8882 {
8883 case value_t::null:
8884 {
8885 if (add_prefix)
8886 {
8887 oa->write_character(to_char_type('Z'));
8888 }
8889 break;
8890 }
8891
8892 case value_t::boolean:
8893 {
8894 if (add_prefix)
8895 {
8896 oa->write_character(j.m_value.boolean
8897 ? to_char_type('T')
8898 : to_char_type('F'));
8899 }
8900 break;
8901 }
8902
8903 case value_t::number_integer:
8904 {
8905 write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(j.m_value.number_integer, add_prefix);
8906 break;
8907 }
8908
8909 case value_t::number_unsigned:
8910 {
8911 write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(j.m_value.number_unsigned, add_prefix);
8912 break;
8913 }
8914
8915 case value_t::number_float:
8916 {
8917 write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(j.m_value.number_float, add_prefix);
8918 break;
8919 }
8920
8921 case value_t::string:
8922 {
8923 if (add_prefix)
8924 {
8925 oa->write_character(to_char_type('S'));
8926 }
8927 write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(j.m_value.string->size(), true);
8928 oa->write_characters(
8929 reinterpret_cast<const CharType*>(j.m_value.string->c_str()),
8930 j.m_value.string->size());
8931 break;
8932 }
8933
8934 case value_t::array:
8935 {
8936 if (add_prefix)
8937 {
8938 oa->write_character(to_char_type('['));
8939 }
8940
8941 bool prefix_required = true;
8942 if (use_type and not j.m_value.array->empty())
8943 {
8944 assert(use_count);
8945 const CharType first_prefix = ubjson_prefix(j.front());
8946 const bool same_prefix = std::all_of(j.begin() + 1, j.end(),
8947 [this, first_prefix](const BasicJsonType & v)
8948 {
8949 return ubjson_prefix(v) == first_prefix;
8950 });
8951
8952 if (same_prefix)
8953 {
8954 prefix_required = false;
8955 oa->write_character(to_char_type('$'));
8956 oa->write_character(first_prefix);
8957 }
8958 }
8959
8960 if (use_count)
8961 {
8962 oa->write_character(to_char_type('#'));
8963 write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(j.m_value.array->size(), true);
8964 }
8965
8966 for (const auto& el : *j.m_value.array)
8967 {
8968 write_ubjson(el, use_count, use_type, prefix_required);
8969 }
8970
8971 if (not use_count)
8972 {
8973 oa->write_character(to_char_type(']'));
8974 }
8975
8976 break;
8977 }
8978
8979 case value_t::object:
8980 {
8981 if (add_prefix)
8982 {
8983 oa->write_character(to_char_type('{'));
8984 }
8985
8986 bool prefix_required = true;
8987 if (use_type and not j.m_value.object->empty())
8988 {
8989 assert(use_count);
8990 const CharType first_prefix = ubjson_prefix(j.front());
8991 const bool same_prefix = std::all_of(j.begin(), j.end(),
8992 [this, first_prefix](const BasicJsonType & v)
8993 {
8994 return ubjson_prefix(v) == first_prefix;
8995 });
8996
8997 if (same_prefix)
8998 {
8999 prefix_required = false;
9000 oa->write_character(to_char_type('$'));
9001 oa->write_character(first_prefix);
9002 }
9003 }
9004
9005 if (use_count)
9006 {
9007 oa->write_character(to_char_type('#'));
9008 write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(j.m_value.object->size(), true);
9009 }
9010
9011 for (const auto& el : *j.m_value.object)
9012 {
9013 write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(el.first.size(), true);
9014 oa->write_characters(
9015 reinterpret_cast<const CharType*>(el.first.c_str()),
9016 el.first.size());
9017 write_ubjson(el.second, use_count, use_type, prefix_required);
9018 }
9019
9020 if (not use_count)
9021 {
9022 oa->write_character(to_char_type('}'));
9023 }
9024
9025 break;
9026 }
9027
9028 default:
9029 break;
9030 }
9031 }
9032
9033 private:
9035 // BSON //
9037
9042 static std::size_t calc_bson_entry_header_size(const string_t& name)
9043 {
9044 const auto it = name.find(static_cast<typename string_t::value_type>(0));
9045 if (JSON_UNLIKELY(it != BasicJsonType::string_t::npos))
9046 {
9047 JSON_THROW(out_of_range::create(409,
9048 "BSON key cannot contain code point U+0000 (at byte " + std::to_string(it) + ")"));
9049 }
9050
9051 return /*id*/ 1ul + name.size() + /*zero-terminator*/1u;
9052 }
9053
9057 void write_bson_entry_header(const string_t& name,
9058 const std::uint8_t element_type)
9059 {
9060 oa->write_character(to_char_type(element_type)); // boolean
9061 oa->write_characters(
9062 reinterpret_cast<const CharType*>(name.c_str()),
9063 name.size() + 1u);
9064 }
9065
9069 void write_bson_boolean(const string_t& name,
9070 const bool value)
9071 {
9072 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x08);
9073 oa->write_character(value ? to_char_type(0x01) : to_char_type(0x00));
9074 }
9075
9079 void write_bson_double(const string_t& name,
9080 const double value)
9081 {
9082 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x01);
9083 write_number<double, true>(value);
9084 }
9085
9089 static std::size_t calc_bson_string_size(const string_t& value)
9090 {
9091 return sizeof(std::int32_t) + value.size() + 1ul;
9092 }
9093
9097 void write_bson_string(const string_t& name,
9098 const string_t& value)
9099 {
9100 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x02);
9101
9102 write_number<std::int32_t, true>(static_cast<std::int32_t>(value.size() + 1ul));
9103 oa->write_characters(
9104 reinterpret_cast<const CharType*>(value.c_str()),
9105 value.size() + 1);
9106 }
9107
9111 void write_bson_null(const string_t& name)
9112 {
9113 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x0A);
9114 }
9115
9119 static std::size_t calc_bson_integer_size(const std::int64_t value)
9120 {
9121 if ((std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::min)() <= value and value <= (std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::max)())
9122 {
9123 return sizeof(std::int32_t);
9124 }
9125 else
9126 {
9127 return sizeof(std::int64_t);
9128 }
9129 }
9130
9134 void write_bson_integer(const string_t& name,
9135 const std::int64_t value)
9136 {
9137 if ((std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::min)() <= value and value <= (std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::max)())
9138 {
9139 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x10); // int32
9140 write_number<std::int32_t, true>(static_cast<std::int32_t>(value));
9141 }
9142 else
9143 {
9144 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x12); // int64
9145 write_number<std::int64_t, true>(static_cast<std::int64_t>(value));
9146 }
9147 }
9148
9152 static constexpr std::size_t calc_bson_unsigned_size(const std::uint64_t value) noexcept
9153 {
9154 return (value <= static_cast<std::uint64_t>((std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::max)()))
9155 ? sizeof(std::int32_t)
9156 : sizeof(std::int64_t);
9157 }
9158
9162 void write_bson_unsigned(const string_t& name,
9163 const std::uint64_t value)
9164 {
9165 if (value <= static_cast<std::uint64_t>((std::numeric_limits<std::int32_t>::max)()))
9166 {
9167 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x10 /* int32 */);
9168 write_number<std::int32_t, true>(static_cast<std::int32_t>(value));
9169 }
9170 else if (value <= static_cast<std::uint64_t>((std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max)()))
9171 {
9172 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x12 /* int64 */);
9173 write_number<std::int64_t, true>(static_cast<std::int64_t>(value));
9174 }
9175 else
9176 {
9177 JSON_THROW(out_of_range::create(407, "integer number " + std::to_string(value) + " cannot be represented by BSON as it does not fit int64"));
9178 }
9179 }
9180
9184 void write_bson_object_entry(const string_t& name,
9185 const typename BasicJsonType::object_t& value)
9186 {
9187 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x03); // object
9188 write_bson_object(value);
9189 }
9190
9194 static std::size_t calc_bson_array_size(const typename BasicJsonType::array_t& value)
9195 {
9196 std::size_t embedded_document_size = 0ul;
9197 std::size_t array_index = 0ul;
9198
9199 for (const auto& el : value)
9200 {
9201 embedded_document_size += calc_bson_element_size(std::to_string(array_index++), el);
9202 }
9203
9204 return sizeof(std::int32_t) + embedded_document_size + 1ul;
9205 }
9206
9210 void write_bson_array(const string_t& name,
9211 const typename BasicJsonType::array_t& value)
9212 {
9213 write_bson_entry_header(name, 0x04); // array
9214 write_number<std::int32_t, true>(static_cast<std::int32_t>(calc_bson_array_size(value)));
9215
9216 std::size_t array_index = 0ul;
9217
9218 for (const auto& el : value)
9219 {
9220 write_bson_element(std::to_string(array_index++), el);
9221 }
9222
9223 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x00));
9224 }
9225
9230 static std::size_t calc_bson_element_size(const string_t& name,
9231 const BasicJsonType& j)
9232 {
9233 const auto header_size = calc_bson_entry_header_size(name);
9234 switch (j.type())
9235 {
9236 case value_t::object:
9237 return header_size + calc_bson_object_size(*j.m_value.object);
9238
9239 case value_t::array:
9240 return header_size + calc_bson_array_size(*j.m_value.array);
9241
9242 case value_t::boolean:
9243 return header_size + 1ul;
9244
9245 case value_t::number_float:
9246 return header_size + 8ul;
9247
9248 case value_t::number_integer:
9249 return header_size + calc_bson_integer_size(j.m_value.number_integer);
9250
9251 case value_t::number_unsigned:
9252 return header_size + calc_bson_unsigned_size(j.m_value.number_unsigned);
9253
9254 case value_t::string:
9255 return header_size + calc_bson_string_size(*j.m_value.string);
9256
9257 case value_t::null:
9258 return header_size + 0ul;
9259
9260 // LCOV_EXCL_START
9261 default:
9262 assert(false);
9263 return 0ul;
9264 // LCOV_EXCL_STOP
9265 };
9266 }
9267
9275 void write_bson_element(const string_t& name,
9276 const BasicJsonType& j)
9277 {
9278 switch (j.type())
9279 {
9280 case value_t::object:
9281 return write_bson_object_entry(name, *j.m_value.object);
9282
9283 case value_t::array:
9284 return write_bson_array(name, *j.m_value.array);
9285
9286 case value_t::boolean:
9287 return write_bson_boolean(name, j.m_value.boolean);
9288
9289 case value_t::number_float:
9290 return write_bson_double(name, j.m_value.number_float);
9291
9292 case value_t::number_integer:
9293 return write_bson_integer(name, j.m_value.number_integer);
9294
9295 case value_t::number_unsigned:
9296 return write_bson_unsigned(name, j.m_value.number_unsigned);
9297
9298 case value_t::string:
9299 return write_bson_string(name, *j.m_value.string);
9300
9301 case value_t::null:
9302 return write_bson_null(name);
9303
9304 // LCOV_EXCL_START
9305 default:
9306 assert(false);
9307 return;
9308 // LCOV_EXCL_STOP
9309 };
9310 }
9311
9318 static std::size_t calc_bson_object_size(const typename BasicJsonType::object_t& value)
9319 {
9320 std::size_t document_size = std::accumulate(value.begin(), value.end(), 0ul,
9321 [](size_t result, const typename BasicJsonType::object_t::value_type & el)
9322 {
9323 return result += calc_bson_element_size(el.first, el.second);
9324 });
9325
9326 return sizeof(std::int32_t) + document_size + 1ul;
9327 }
9328
9333 void write_bson_object(const typename BasicJsonType::object_t& value)
9334 {
9335 write_number<std::int32_t, true>(static_cast<std::int32_t>(calc_bson_object_size(value)));
9336
9337 for (const auto& el : value)
9338 {
9339 write_bson_element(el.first, el.second);
9340 }
9341
9342 oa->write_character(to_char_type(0x00));
9343 }

9377 // UBJSON: write number (floating point)
9378 template<typename NumberType, typename std::enable_if<
9379 std::is_floating_point<NumberType>::value, int>::type = 0>
9380 void write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(const NumberType n,
9381 const bool add_prefix)
9382 {
9383 if (add_prefix)
9384 {
9385 oa->write_character(get_ubjson_float_prefix(n));
9386 }
9387 write_number(n);

9390 // UBJSON: write number (unsigned integer)
9391 template<typename NumberType, typename std::enable_if<
9392 std::is_unsigned<NumberType>::value, int>::type = 0>
9393 void write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(const NumberType n,
9394 const bool add_prefix)
9395 {
9396 if (n <= static_cast<uint64_t>((std::numeric_limits<int8_t>::max)()))
9397 {
9398 if (add_prefix)
9399 {
9400 oa->write_character(to_char_type('i')); // int8
9401 }
9402 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(n));
9403 }
9404 else if (n <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
9405 {
9406 if (add_prefix)
9407 {
9408 oa->write_character(to_char_type('U')); // uint8
9409 }
9410 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(n));
9411 }
9412 else if (n <= static_cast<uint64_t>((std::numeric_limits<int16_t>::max)()))
9413 {
9414 if (add_prefix)
9415 {
9416 oa->write_character(to_char_type('I')); // int16
9417 }
9418 write_number(static_cast<int16_t>(n));
9419 }
9420 else if (n <= static_cast<uint64_t>((std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max)()))
9421 {
9422 if (add_prefix)
9423 {
9424 oa->write_character(to_char_type('l')); // int32
9425 }
9426 write_number(static_cast<int32_t>(n));
9427 }
9428 else if (n <= static_cast<uint64_t>((std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max)()))
9429 {
9430 if (add_prefix)
9431 {
9432 oa->write_character(to_char_type('L')); // int64
9433 }
9434 write_number(static_cast<int64_t>(n));
9435 }
9436 else
9437 {
9438 JSON_THROW(out_of_range::create(407, "integer number " + std::to_string(n) + " cannot be represented by UBJSON as it does not fit int64"));
9439 }
9440 }
9441
9442 // UBJSON: write number (signed integer)
9443 template<typename NumberType, typename std::enable_if<
9444 std::is_signed<NumberType>::value and
9445 not std::is_floating_point<NumberType>::value, int>::type = 0>
9446 void write_number_with_ubjson_prefix(const NumberType n,
9447 const bool add_prefix)
9448 {
9449 if ((std::numeric_limits<int8_t>::min)() <= n and n <= (std::numeric_limits<int8_t>::max)())
9450 {
9451 if (add_prefix)
9452 {
9453 oa->write_character(to_char_type('i')); // int8
9454 }
9455 write_number(static_cast<int8_t>(n));
9456 }
9457 else if (static_cast<int64_t>((std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::min)()) <= n and n <= static_cast<int64_t>((std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)()))
9458 {
9459 if (add_prefix)
9460 {
9461 oa->write_character(to_char_type('U')); // uint8
9462 }
9463 write_number(static_cast<uint8_t>(n));
9464 }
9465 else if ((std::numeric_limits<int16_t>::min)() <= n and n <= (std::numeric_limits<int16_t>::max)())
9466 {
9467 if (add_prefix)
9468 {
9469 oa->write_character(to_char_type('I')); // int16
9470 }
9471 write_number(static_cast<int16_t>(n));
9472 }
9473 else if ((std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::min)() <= n and n <= (std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max)())
9474 {
9475 if (add_prefix)
9476 {
9477 oa->write_character(to_char_type('l')); // int32
9478 }
9479 write_number(static_cast<int32_t>(n));
9480 }
9481 else if ((std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::min)() <= n and n <= (std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max)())
9482 {
9483 if (add_prefix)
9484 {
9485 oa->write_character(to_char_type('L')); // int64
9486 }
9487 write_number(static_cast<int64_t>(n));
9488 }
9489 // LCOV_EXCL_START
9490 else
9491 {
9492 JSON_THROW(out_of_range::create(407, "integer number " + std::to_string(n) + " cannot be represented by UBJSON as it does not fit int64"));
9493 }

9495 }
9496
9506 CharType ubjson_prefix(const BasicJsonType& j) const noexcept
9507 {
9508 switch (j.type())
9509 {
9510 case value_t::null:
9511 return 'Z';
9512
9513 case value_t::boolean:
9514 return j.m_value.boolean ? 'T' : 'F';
9515
9516 case value_t::number_integer:
9517 {
9518 if ((std::numeric_limits<int8_t>::min)() <= j.m_value.number_integer and j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<int8_t>::max)())
9519 {
9520 return 'i';
9521 }
9522 if ((std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::min)() <= j.m_value.number_integer and j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
9523 {
9524 return 'U';
9525 }
9526 if ((std::numeric_limits<int16_t>::min)() <= j.m_value.number_integer and j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<int16_t>::max)())
9527 {
9528 return 'I';
9529 }
9530 if ((std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::min)() <= j.m_value.number_integer and j.m_value.number_integer <= (std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max)())
9531 {
9532 return 'l';
9533 }
9534 // no check and assume int64_t (see note above)
9535 return 'L';
9536 }
9537
9538 case value_t::number_unsigned:
9539 {
9540 if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<int8_t>::max)())
9541 {
9542 return 'i';
9543 }
9544 if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<uint8_t>::max)())
9545 {
9546 return 'U';
9547 }
9548 if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<int16_t>::max)())
9549 {
9550 return 'I';
9551 }
9552 if (j.m_value.number_unsigned <= (std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max)())
9553 {
9554 return 'l';
9555 }
9556 // no check and assume int64_t (see note above)
9557 return 'L';
9558 }
9559
9560 case value_t::number_float:
9561 return get_ubjson_float_prefix(j.m_value.number_float);
9562
9563 case value_t::string:
9564 return 'S';
9565
9566 case value_t::array:
9567 return '[';
9568
9569 case value_t::object:
9570 return '{';
9571
9572 default: // discarded values
9573 return 'N';
9574 }
9575 }
9576
9577 static constexpr CharType get_ubjson_float_prefix(float /*unused*/)
9578 {
9579 return 'd'; // float 32
9580 }
9581
9582 static constexpr CharType get_ubjson_float_prefix(double /*unused*/)
9583 {
9584 return 'D'; // float 64
9585 }
9586
9588 // Utility functions //
9590
9591 /*
9592 @brief write a number to output input
9593 @param[in] n number of type @a NumberType
9594 @tparam NumberType the type of the number
9595 @tparam OutputIsLittleEndian Set to true if output data is
9596 required to be little endian
9597
9598 @note This function needs to respect the system's endianess, because bytes
9599 in CBOR, MessagePack, and UBJSON are stored in network order (big
9600 endian) and therefore need reordering on little endian systems.
9601 */
9602 template<typename NumberType, bool OutputIsLittleEndian = false>
9603 void write_number(const NumberType n)
9604 {
9605 // step 1: write number to array of length NumberType
9606 std::array<CharType, sizeof(NumberType)> vec;
9607 std::memcpy(vec.data(), &n, sizeof(NumberType));
9608
9609 // step 2: write array to output (with possible reordering)
9610 if (is_little_endian and not OutputIsLittleEndian)
9611 {
9612 // reverse byte order prior to conversion if necessary
9613 std::reverse(vec.begin(), vec.end());
9614 }
9615
9616 oa->write_characters(vec.data(), sizeof(NumberType));
9617 }
9618
9619 public:
9620 // The following to_char_type functions are implement the conversion
9621 // between uint8_t and CharType. In case CharType is not unsigned,
9622 // such a conversion is required to allow values greater than 128.
9623 // See <https://github.com/nlohmann/json/issues/1286> for a discussion.
9624 template < typename C = CharType,
9625 enable_if_t < std::is_signed<C>::value and std::is_signed<char>::value > * = nullptr >
9626 static constexpr CharType to_char_type(std::uint8_t x) noexcept
9627 {
9628 return *reinterpret_cast<char*>(&x);
9629 }
9630
9631 template < typename C = CharType,
9632 enable_if_t < std::is_signed<C>::value and std::is_unsigned<char>::value > * = nullptr >
9633 static CharType to_char_type(std::uint8_t x) noexcept
9634 {
9635 static_assert(sizeof(std::uint8_t) == sizeof(CharType), "size of CharType must be equal to std::uint8_t");
9636 static_assert(std::is_pod<CharType>::value, "CharType must be POD");
9637 CharType result;
9638 std::memcpy(&result, &x, sizeof(x));
9639 return result;
9640 }
9641
9642 template<typename C = CharType,
9643 enable_if_t<std::is_unsigned<C>::value>* = nullptr>
9644 static constexpr CharType to_char_type(std::uint8_t x) noexcept
9645 {
9646 return x;
9647 }
9648
9649 template < typename InputCharType, typename C = CharType,
9650 enable_if_t <
9651 std::is_signed<C>::value and
9652 std::is_signed<char>::value and
9653 std::is_same<char, typename std::remove_cv<InputCharType>::type>::value
9654 > * = nullptr >
9655 static constexpr CharType to_char_type(InputCharType x) noexcept
9656 {
9657 return x;
9658 }
9659
9660 private:
9662 const bool is_little_endian = binary_reader<BasicJsonType>::little_endianess();
9663
9665 output_adapter_t<CharType> oa = nullptr;
9666};

9724template <typename Target, typename Source>
9725Target reinterpret_bits(const Source source)
9726{
9727 static_assert(sizeof(Target) == sizeof(Source), "size mismatch");
9728
9729 Target target;
9730 std::memcpy(&target, &source, sizeof(Source));
9731 return target;

9733
9734struct diyfp // f * 2^e
9735{
9736 static constexpr int kPrecision = 64; // = q
9737
9738 uint64_t f = 0;
9739 int e = 0;
9740
9741 constexpr diyfp(uint64_t f_, int e_) noexcept : f(f_), e(e_) {}
9742
9747 static diyfp sub(const diyfp& x, const diyfp& y) noexcept
9748 {
9749 assert(x.e == y.e);
9750 assert(x.f >= y.f);
9751
9752 return {x.f - y.f, x.e};
9753 }
9754
9759 static diyfp mul(const diyfp& x, const diyfp& y) noexcept
9760 {
9761 static_assert(kPrecision == 64, "internal error");
9762
9763 // Computes:
9764 // f = round((x.f * y.f) / 2^q)
9765 // e = x.e + y.e + q
9766
9767 // Emulate the 64-bit * 64-bit multiplication:
9768 //
9769 // p = u * v
9770 // = (u_lo + 2^32 u_hi) (v_lo + 2^32 v_hi)
9771 // = (u_lo v_lo ) + 2^32 ((u_lo v_hi ) + (u_hi v_lo )) + 2^64 (u_hi v_hi )
9772 // = (p0 ) + 2^32 ((p1 ) + (p2 )) + 2^64 (p3 )
9773 // = (p0_lo + 2^32 p0_hi) + 2^32 ((p1_lo + 2^32 p1_hi) + (p2_lo + 2^32 p2_hi)) + 2^64 (p3 )
9774 // = (p0_lo ) + 2^32 (p0_hi + p1_lo + p2_lo ) + 2^64 (p1_hi + p2_hi + p3)
9775 // = (p0_lo ) + 2^32 (Q ) + 2^64 (H )
9776 // = (p0_lo ) + 2^32 (Q_lo + 2^32 Q_hi ) + 2^64 (H )
9777 //
9778 // (Since Q might be larger than 2^32 - 1)
9779 //
9780 // = (p0_lo + 2^32 Q_lo) + 2^64 (Q_hi + H)
9781 //
9782 // (Q_hi + H does not overflow a 64-bit int)
9783 //
9784 // = p_lo + 2^64 p_hi
9785
9786 const uint64_t u_lo = x.f & 0xFFFFFFFF;
9787 const uint64_t u_hi = x.f >> 32;
9788 const uint64_t v_lo = y.f & 0xFFFFFFFF;
9789 const uint64_t v_hi = y.f >> 32;
9790
9791 const uint64_t p0 = u_lo * v_lo;
9792 const uint64_t p1 = u_lo * v_hi;
9793 const uint64_t p2 = u_hi * v_lo;
9794 const uint64_t p3 = u_hi * v_hi;
9795
9796 const uint64_t p0_hi = p0 >> 32;
9797 const uint64_t p1_lo = p1 & 0xFFFFFFFF;
9798 const uint64_t p1_hi = p1 >> 32;
9799 const uint64_t p2_lo = p2 & 0xFFFFFFFF;
9800 const uint64_t p2_hi = p2 >> 32;
9801
9802 uint64_t Q = p0_hi + p1_lo + p2_lo;
9803
9804 // The full product might now be computed as
9805 //
9806 // p_hi = p3 + p2_hi + p1_hi + (Q >> 32)
9807 // p_lo = p0_lo + (Q << 32)
9808 //
9809 // But in this particular case here, the full p_lo is not required.
9810 // Effectively we only need to add the highest bit in p_lo to p_hi (and
9811 // Q_hi + 1 does not overflow).
9812
9813 Q += uint64_t{1} << (64 - 32 - 1); // round, ties up
9814
9815 const uint64_t h = p3 + p2_hi + p1_hi + (Q >> 32);
9816
9817 return {h, x.e + y.e + 64};
9818 }
9819
9824 static diyfp normalize(diyfp x) noexcept
9825 {
9826 assert(x.f != 0);
9827
9828 while ((x.f >> 63) == 0)
9829 {
9830 x.f <<= 1;
9831 x.e--;
9832 }
9833
9834 return x;
9835 }
9836
9841 static diyfp normalize_to(const diyfp& x, const int target_exponent) noexcept
9842 {
9843 const int delta = x.e - target_exponent;
9844
9845 assert(delta >= 0);
9846 assert(((x.f << delta) >> delta) == x.f);
9847
9848 return {x.f << delta, target_exponent};
9849 }
9850};
9851
9852struct boundaries
9853{
9854 diyfp w;
9855 diyfp minus;
9856 diyfp plus;
9857};
9858
9865template <typename FloatType>
9866boundaries compute_boundaries(FloatType value)
9867{
9868 assert(std::isfinite(value));
9869 assert(value > 0);
9870
9871 // Convert the IEEE representation into a diyfp.
9872 //
9873 // If v is denormal:
9874 // value = 0.F * 2^(1 - bias) = ( F) * 2^(1 - bias - (p-1))
9875 // If v is normalized:
9876 // value = 1.F * 2^(E - bias) = (2^(p-1) + F) * 2^(E - bias - (p-1))
9877
9878 static_assert(std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::is_iec559,
9879 "internal error: dtoa_short requires an IEEE-754 floating-point implementation");
9880
9881 constexpr int kPrecision = std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::digits; // = p (includes the hidden bit)
9882 constexpr int kBias = std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::max_exponent - 1 + (kPrecision - 1);
9883 constexpr int kMinExp = 1 - kBias;
9884 constexpr uint64_t kHiddenBit = uint64_t{1} << (kPrecision - 1); // = 2^(p-1)
9885
9886 using bits_type = typename std::conditional< kPrecision == 24, uint32_t, uint64_t >::type;
9887
9888 const uint64_t bits = reinterpret_bits<bits_type>(value);
9889 const uint64_t E = bits >> (kPrecision - 1);
9890 const uint64_t F = bits & (kHiddenBit - 1);
9891
9892 const bool is_denormal = (E == 0);
9893 const diyfp v = is_denormal
9894 ? diyfp(F, kMinExp)
9895 : diyfp(F + kHiddenBit, static_cast<int>(E) - kBias);
9896
9897 // Compute the boundaries m- and m+ of the floating-point value
9898 // v = f * 2^e.
9899 //
9900 // Determine v- and v+, the floating-point predecessor and successor if v,
9901 // respectively.
9902 //
9903 // v- = v - 2^e if f != 2^(p-1) or e == e_min (A)
9904 // = v - 2^(e-1) if f == 2^(p-1) and e > e_min (B)
9905 //
9906 // v+ = v + 2^e
9907 //
9908 // Let m- = (v- + v) / 2 and m+ = (v + v+) / 2. All real numbers _strictly_
9909 // between m- and m+ round to v, regardless of how the input rounding
9910 // algorithm breaks ties.
9911 //
9912 // ---+-------------+-------------+-------------+-------------+--- (A)
9913 // v- m- v m+ v+
9914 //
9915 // -----------------+------+------+-------------+-------------+--- (B)
9916 // v- m- v m+ v+
9917
9918 const bool lower_boundary_is_closer = (F == 0 and E > 1);
9919 const diyfp m_plus = diyfp(2 * v.f + 1, v.e - 1);
9920 const diyfp m_minus = lower_boundary_is_closer
9921 ? diyfp(4 * v.f - 1, v.e - 2) // (B)
9922 : diyfp(2 * v.f - 1, v.e - 1); // (A)
9923
9924 // Determine the normalized w+ = m+.
9925 const diyfp w_plus = diyfp::normalize(m_plus);
9926
9927 // Determine w- = m- such that e_(w-) = e_(w+).
9928 const diyfp w_minus = diyfp::normalize_to(m_minus, w_plus.e);
9929
9930 return {diyfp::normalize(v), w_minus, w_plus};
9931}
9932
9933// Given normalized diyfp w, Grisu needs to find a (normalized) cached
9934// power-of-ten c, such that the exponent of the product c * w = f * 2^e lies
9935// within a certain range [alpha, gamma] (Definition 3.2 from [1])
9936//
9937// alpha <= e = e_c + e_w + q <= gamma
9938//
9939// or
9940//
9941// f_c * f_w * 2^alpha <= f_c 2^(e_c) * f_w 2^(e_w) * 2^q
9942// <= f_c * f_w * 2^gamma
9943//
9944// Since c and w are normalized, i.e. 2^(q-1) <= f < 2^q, this implies
9945//
9946// 2^(q-1) * 2^(q-1) * 2^alpha <= c * w * 2^q < 2^q * 2^q * 2^gamma
9947//
9948// or
9949//
9950// 2^(q - 2 + alpha) <= c * w < 2^(q + gamma)
9951//
9952// The choice of (alpha,gamma) determines the size of the table and the form of
9953// the digit generation procedure. Using (alpha,gamma)=(-60,-32) works out well
9954// in practice:
9955//
9956// The idea is to cut the number c * w = f * 2^e into two parts, which can be
9957// processed independently: An integral part p1, and a fractional part p2:
9958//
9959// f * 2^e = ( (f div 2^-e) * 2^-e + (f mod 2^-e) ) * 2^e
9960// = (f div 2^-e) + (f mod 2^-e) * 2^e
9961// = p1 + p2 * 2^e
9962//
9963// The conversion of p1 into decimal form requires a series of divisions and
9964// modulos by (a power of) 10. These operations are faster for 32-bit than for
9965// 64-bit integers, so p1 should ideally fit into a 32-bit integer. This can be
9966// achieved by choosing
9967//
9968// -e >= 32 or e <= -32 := gamma
9969//
9970// In order to convert the fractional part
9971//
9972// p2 * 2^e = p2 / 2^-e = d[-1] / 10^1 + d[-2] / 10^2 + ...
9973//
9974// into decimal form, the fraction is repeatedly multiplied by 10 and the digits
9975// d[-i] are extracted in order:
9976//
9977// (10 * p2) div 2^-e = d[-1]
9978// (10 * p2) mod 2^-e = d[-2] / 10^1 + ...
9979//
9980// The multiplication by 10 must not overflow. It is sufficient to choose
9981//
9982// 10 * p2 < 16 * p2 = 2^4 * p2 <= 2^64.
9983//
9984// Since p2 = f mod 2^-e < 2^-e,
9985//
9986// -e <= 60 or e >= -60 := alpha
9987
9988constexpr int kAlpha = -60;
9989constexpr int kGamma = -32;
9990
9991struct cached_power // c = f * 2^e ~= 10^k
9992{
9993 uint64_t f;
9994 int e;
9995 int k;
9996};
9997
10005inline cached_power get_cached_power_for_binary_exponent(int e)
10006{
10007 // Now
10008 //
10009 // alpha <= e_c + e + q <= gamma (1)
10010 // ==> f_c * 2^alpha <= c * 2^e * 2^q
10011 //
10012 // and since the c's are normalized, 2^(q-1) <= f_c,
10013 //
10014 // ==> 2^(q - 1 + alpha) <= c * 2^(e + q)
10015 // ==> 2^(alpha - e - 1) <= c
10016 //
10017 // If c were an exakt power of ten, i.e. c = 10^k, one may determine k as
10018 //
10019 // k = ceil( log_10( 2^(alpha - e - 1) ) )
10020 // = ceil( (alpha - e - 1) * log_10(2) )
10021 //
10022 // From the paper:
10023 // "In theory the result of the procedure could be wrong since c is rounded,
10024 // and the computation itself is approximated [...]. In practice, however,
10025 // this simple function is sufficient."
10026 //
10027 // For IEEE double precision floating-point numbers converted into
10028 // normalized diyfp's w = f * 2^e, with q = 64,
10029 //
10030 // e >= -1022 (min IEEE exponent)
10031 // -52 (p - 1)
10032 // -52 (p - 1, possibly normalize denormal IEEE numbers)
10033 // -11 (normalize the diyfp)
10034 // = -1137
10035 //
10036 // and
10037 //
10038 // e <= +1023 (max IEEE exponent)
10039 // -52 (p - 1)
10040 // -11 (normalize the diyfp)
10041 // = 960
10042 //
10043 // This binary exponent range [-1137,960] results in a decimal exponent
10044 // range [-307,324]. One does not need to store a cached power for each
10045 // k in this range. For each such k it suffices to find a cached power
10046 // such that the exponent of the product lies in [alpha,gamma].
10047 // This implies that the difference of the decimal exponents of adjacent
10048 // table entries must be less than or equal to
10049 //
10050 // floor( (gamma - alpha) * log_10(2) ) = 8.
10051 //
10052 // (A smaller distance gamma-alpha would require a larger table.)
10053
10054 // NB:
10055 // Actually this function returns c, such that -60 <= e_c + e + 64 <= -34.
10056
10057 constexpr int kCachedPowersSize = 79;
10058 constexpr int kCachedPowersMinDecExp = -300;
10059 constexpr int kCachedPowersDecStep = 8;
10060
10061 static constexpr cached_power kCachedPowers[] =
10062 {
10063 { 0xAB70FE17C79AC6CA, -1060, -300 },
10064 { 0xFF77B1FCBEBCDC4F, -1034, -292 },
10065 { 0xBE5691EF416BD60C, -1007, -284 },
10066 { 0x8DD01FAD907FFC3C, -980, -276 },
10067 { 0xD3515C2831559A83, -954, -268 },
10068 { 0x9D71AC8FADA6C9B5, -927, -260 },
10069 { 0xEA9C227723EE8BCB, -901, -252 },
10070 { 0xAECC49914078536D, -874, -244 },
10071 { 0x823C12795DB6CE57, -847, -236 },
10072 { 0xC21094364DFB5637, -821, -228 },
10073 { 0x9096EA6F3848984F, -794, -220 },
10074 { 0xD77485CB25823AC7, -768, -212 },
10075 { 0xA086CFCD97BF97F4, -741, -204 },
10076 { 0xEF340A98172AACE5, -715, -196 },
10077 { 0xB23867FB2A35B28E, -688, -188 },
10078 { 0x84C8D4DFD2C63F3B, -661, -180 },
10079 { 0xC5DD44271AD3CDBA, -635, -172 },
10080 { 0x936B9FCEBB25C996, -608, -164 },
10081 { 0xDBAC6C247D62A584, -582, -156 },
10082 { 0xA3AB66580D5FDAF6, -555, -148 },
10083 { 0xF3E2F893DEC3F126, -529, -140 },
10084 { 0xB5B5ADA8AAFF80B8, -502, -132 },
10085 { 0x87625F056C7C4A8B, -475, -124 },
10086 { 0xC9BCFF6034C13053, -449, -116 },
10087 { 0x964E858C91BA2655, -422, -108 },
10088 { 0xDFF9772470297EBD, -396, -100 },
10089 { 0xA6DFBD9FB8E5B88F, -369, -92 },
10090 { 0xF8A95FCF88747D94, -343, -84 },
10091 { 0xB94470938FA89BCF, -316, -76 },
10092 { 0x8A08F0F8BF0F156B, -289, -68 },
10093 { 0xCDB02555653131B6, -263, -60 },
10094 { 0x993FE2C6D07B7FAC, -236, -52 },
10095 { 0xE45C10C42A2B3B06, -210, -44 },
10096 { 0xAA242499697392D3, -183, -36 },
10097 { 0xFD87B5F28300CA0E, -157, -28 },
10098 { 0xBCE5086492111AEB, -130, -20 },
10099 { 0x8CBCCC096F5088CC, -103, -12 },
10100 { 0xD1B71758E219652C, -77, -4 },
10101 { 0x9C40000000000000, -50, 4 },
10102 { 0xE8D4A51000000000, -24, 12 },
10103 { 0xAD78EBC5AC620000, 3, 20 },
10104 { 0x813F3978F8940984, 30, 28 },
10105 { 0xC097CE7BC90715B3, 56, 36 },
10106 { 0x8F7E32CE7BEA5C70, 83, 44 },
10107 { 0xD5D238A4ABE98068, 109, 52 },
10108 { 0x9F4F2726179A2245, 136, 60 },
10109 { 0xED63A231D4C4FB27, 162, 68 },
10110 { 0xB0DE65388CC8ADA8, 189, 76 },
10111 { 0x83C7088E1AAB65DB, 216, 84 },
10112 { 0xC45D1DF942711D9A, 242, 92 },
10113 { 0x924D692CA61BE758, 269, 100 },
10114 { 0xDA01EE641A708DEA, 295, 108 },
10115 { 0xA26DA3999AEF774A, 322, 116 },
10116 { 0xF209787BB47D6B85, 348, 124 },
10117 { 0xB454E4A179DD1877, 375, 132 },
10118 { 0x865B86925B9BC5C2, 402, 140 },
10119 { 0xC83553C5C8965D3D, 428, 148 },
10120 { 0x952AB45CFA97A0B3, 455, 156 },
10121 { 0xDE469FBD99A05FE3, 481, 164 },
10122 { 0xA59BC234DB398C25, 508, 172 },
10123 { 0xF6C69A72A3989F5C, 534, 180 },
10124 { 0xB7DCBF5354E9BECE, 561, 188 },
10125 { 0x88FCF317F22241E2, 588, 196 },
10126 { 0xCC20CE9BD35C78A5, 614, 204 },
10127 { 0x98165AF37B2153DF, 641, 212 },
10128 { 0xE2A0B5DC971F303A, 667, 220 },
10129 { 0xA8D9D1535CE3B396, 694, 228 },
10130 { 0xFB9B7CD9A4A7443C, 720, 236 },
10131 { 0xBB764C4CA7A44410, 747, 244 },
10132 { 0x8BAB8EEFB6409C1A, 774, 252 },
10133 { 0xD01FEF10A657842C, 800, 260 },
10134 { 0x9B10A4E5E9913129, 827, 268 },
10135 { 0xE7109BFBA19C0C9D, 853, 276 },
10136 { 0xAC2820D9623BF429, 880, 284 },
10137 { 0x80444B5E7AA7CF85, 907, 292 },
10138 { 0xBF21E44003ACDD2D, 933, 300 },
10139 { 0x8E679C2F5E44FF8F, 960, 308 },
10140 { 0xD433179D9C8CB841, 986, 316 },
10141 { 0x9E19DB92B4E31BA9, 1013, 324 },
10142 };
10143
10144 // This computation gives exactly the same results for k as
10145 // k = ceil((kAlpha - e - 1) * 0.30102999566398114)
10146 // for |e| <= 1500, but doesn't require floating-point operations.
10147 // NB: log_10(2) ~= 78913 / 2^18
10148 assert(e >= -1500);
10149 assert(e <= 1500);
10150 const int f = kAlpha - e - 1;
10151 const int k = (f * 78913) / (1 << 18) + static_cast<int>(f > 0);
10152
10153 const int index = (-kCachedPowersMinDecExp + k + (kCachedPowersDecStep - 1)) / kCachedPowersDecStep;
10154 assert(index >= 0);
10155 assert(index < kCachedPowersSize);
10156 static_cast<void>(kCachedPowersSize); // Fix warning.
10157
10158 const cached_power cached = kCachedPowers[index];
10159 assert(kAlpha <= cached.e + e + 64);
10160 assert(kGamma >= cached.e + e + 64);
10161
10162 return cached;
10163}
10164
10169inline int find_largest_pow10(const uint32_t n, uint32_t& pow10)
10170{
10171 // LCOV_EXCL_START
10172 if (n >= 1000000000)
10173 {
10174 pow10 = 1000000000;
10175 return 10;
10176 }
10177 // LCOV_EXCL_STOP
10178 else if (n >= 100000000)
10179 {
10180 pow10 = 100000000;
10181 return 9;
10182 }
10183 else if (n >= 10000000)
10184 {
10185 pow10 = 10000000;
10186 return 8;
10187 }
10188 else if (n >= 1000000)
10189 {
10190 pow10 = 1000000;
10191 return 7;
10192 }
10193 else if (n >= 100000)
10194 {
10195 pow10 = 100000;
10196 return 6;
10197 }
10198 else if (n >= 10000)
10199 {
10200 pow10 = 10000;
10201 return 5;
10202 }
10203 else if (n >= 1000)
10204 {
10205 pow10 = 1000;
10206 return 4;
10207 }
10208 else if (n >= 100)
10209 {
10210 pow10 = 100;
10211 return 3;
10212 }
10213 else if (n >= 10)
10214 {
10215 pow10 = 10;
10216 return 2;
10217 }
10218 else
10219 {
10220 pow10 = 1;
10221 return 1;
10222 }
10223}
10224
10225inline void grisu2_round(char* buf, int len, uint64_t dist, uint64_t delta,
10226 uint64_t rest, uint64_t ten_k)
10227{
10228 assert(len >= 1);
10229 assert(dist <= delta);
10230 assert(rest <= delta);
10231 assert(ten_k > 0);
10232
10233 // <--------------------------- delta ---->
10234 // <---- dist --------->
10235 // --------------[------------------+-------------------]--------------
10236 // M- w M+
10237 //
10238 // ten_k
10239 // <------>
10240 // <---- rest ---->
10241 // --------------[------------------+----+--------------]--------------
10242 // w V
10243 // = buf * 10^k
10244 //
10245 // ten_k represents a unit-in-the-last-place in the decimal representation
10246 // stored in buf.
10247 // Decrement buf by ten_k while this takes buf closer to w.
10248
10249 // The tests are written in this order to avoid overflow in unsigned
10250 // integer arithmetic.
10251
10252 while (rest < dist
10253 and delta - rest >= ten_k
10254 and (rest + ten_k < dist or dist - rest > rest + ten_k - dist))
10255 {
10256 assert(buf[len - 1] != '0');
10257 buf[len - 1]--;
10258 rest += ten_k;
10259 }
10260}
10261
10266inline void grisu2_digit_gen(char* buffer, int& length, int& decimal_exponent,
10267 diyfp M_minus, diyfp w, diyfp M_plus)
10268{
10269 static_assert(kAlpha >= -60, "internal error");
10270 static_assert(kGamma <= -32, "internal error");
10271
10272 // Generates the digits (and the exponent) of a decimal floating-point
10273 // number V = buffer * 10^decimal_exponent in the range [M-, M+]. The diyfp's
10274 // w, M- and M+ share the same exponent e, which satisfies alpha <= e <= gamma.
10275 //
10276 // <--------------------------- delta ---->
10277 // <---- dist --------->
10278 // --------------[------------------+-------------------]--------------
10279 // M- w M+
10280 //
10281 // Grisu2 generates the digits of M+ from left to right and stops as soon as
10282 // V is in [M-,M+].
10283
10284 assert(M_plus.e >= kAlpha);
10285 assert(M_plus.e <= kGamma);
10286
10287 uint64_t delta = diyfp::sub(M_plus, M_minus).f; // (significand of (M+ - M-), implicit exponent is e)
10288 uint64_t dist = diyfp::sub(M_plus, w ).f; // (significand of (M+ - w ), implicit exponent is e)
10289
10290 // Split M+ = f * 2^e into two parts p1 and p2 (note: e < 0):
10291 //
10292 // M+ = f * 2^e
10293 // = ((f div 2^-e) * 2^-e + (f mod 2^-e)) * 2^e
10294 // = ((p1 ) * 2^-e + (p2 )) * 2^e
10295 // = p1 + p2 * 2^e
10296
10297 const diyfp one(uint64_t{1} << -M_plus.e, M_plus.e);
10298
10299 auto p1 = static_cast<uint32_t>(M_plus.f >> -one.e); // p1 = f div 2^-e (Since -e >= 32, p1 fits into a 32-bit int.)
10300 uint64_t p2 = M_plus.f & (one.f - 1); // p2 = f mod 2^-e
10301
10302 // 1)
10303 //
10304 // Generate the digits of the integral part p1 = d[n-1]...d[1]d[0]
10305
10306 assert(p1 > 0);
10307
10308 uint32_t pow10;
10309 const int k = find_largest_pow10(p1, pow10);
10310
10311 // 10^(k-1) <= p1 < 10^k, pow10 = 10^(k-1)
10312 //
10313 // p1 = (p1 div 10^(k-1)) * 10^(k-1) + (p1 mod 10^(k-1))
10314 // = (d[k-1] ) * 10^(k-1) + (p1 mod 10^(k-1))
10315 //
10316 // M+ = p1 + p2 * 2^e
10317 // = d[k-1] * 10^(k-1) + (p1 mod 10^(k-1)) + p2 * 2^e
10318 // = d[k-1] * 10^(k-1) + ((p1 mod 10^(k-1)) * 2^-e + p2) * 2^e
10319 // = d[k-1] * 10^(k-1) + ( rest) * 2^e
10320 //
10321 // Now generate the digits d[n] of p1 from left to right (n = k-1,...,0)
10322 //
10323 // p1 = d[k-1]...d[n] * 10^n + d[n-1]...d[0]
10324 //
10325 // but stop as soon as
10326 //
10327 // rest * 2^e = (d[n-1]...d[0] * 2^-e + p2) * 2^e <= delta * 2^e
10328
10329 int n = k;
10330 while (n > 0)
10331 {
10332 // Invariants:
10333 // M+ = buffer * 10^n + (p1 + p2 * 2^e) (buffer = 0 for n = k)
10334 // pow10 = 10^(n-1) <= p1 < 10^n
10335 //
10336 const uint32_t d = p1 / pow10; // d = p1 div 10^(n-1)
10337 const uint32_t r = p1 % pow10; // r = p1 mod 10^(n-1)
10338 //
10339 // M+ = buffer * 10^n + (d * 10^(n-1) + r) + p2 * 2^e
10340 // = (buffer * 10 + d) * 10^(n-1) + (r + p2 * 2^e)
10341 //
10342 assert(d <= 9);
10343 buffer[length++] = static_cast<char>('0' + d); // buffer := buffer * 10 + d
10344 //
10345 // M+ = buffer * 10^(n-1) + (r + p2 * 2^e)
10346 //
10347 p1 = r;
10348 n--;
10349 //
10350 // M+ = buffer * 10^n + (p1 + p2 * 2^e)
10351 // pow10 = 10^n
10352 //
10353
10354 // Now check if enough digits have been generated.
10355 // Compute
10356 //
10357 // p1 + p2 * 2^e = (p1 * 2^-e + p2) * 2^e = rest * 2^e
10358 //
10359 // Note:
10360 // Since rest and delta share the same exponent e, it suffices to
10361 // compare the significands.
10362 const uint64_t rest = (uint64_t{p1} << -one.e) + p2;
10363 if (rest <= delta)
10364 {
10365 // V = buffer * 10^n, with M- <= V <= M+.
10366
10367 decimal_exponent += n;
10368
10369 // We may now just stop. But instead look if the buffer could be
10370 // decremented to bring V closer to w.
10371 //
10372 // pow10 = 10^n is now 1 ulp in the decimal representation V.
10373 // The rounding procedure works with diyfp's with an implicit
10374 // exponent of e.
10375 //
10376 // 10^n = (10^n * 2^-e) * 2^e = ulp * 2^e
10377 //
10378 const uint64_t ten_n = uint64_t{pow10} << -one.e;
10379 grisu2_round(buffer, length, dist, delta, rest, ten_n);
10380
10381 return;
10382 }
10383
10384 pow10 /= 10;
10385 //
10386 // pow10 = 10^(n-1) <= p1 < 10^n
10387 // Invariants restored.
10388 }
10389
10390 // 2)
10391 //
10392 // The digits of the integral part have been generated:
10393 //
10394 // M+ = d[k-1]...d[1]d[0] + p2 * 2^e
10395 // = buffer + p2 * 2^e
10396 //
10397 // Now generate the digits of the fractional part p2 * 2^e.
10398 //
10399 // Note:
10400 // No decimal point is generated: the exponent is adjusted instead.
10401 //
10402 // p2 actually represents the fraction
10403 //
10404 // p2 * 2^e
10405 // = p2 / 2^-e
10406 // = d[-1] / 10^1 + d[-2] / 10^2 + ...
10407 //
10408 // Now generate the digits d[-m] of p1 from left to right (m = 1,2,...)
10409 //
10410 // p2 * 2^e = d[-1]d[-2]...d[-m] * 10^-m
10411 // + 10^-m * (d[-m-1] / 10^1 + d[-m-2] / 10^2 + ...)
10412 //
10413 // using
10414 //
10415 // 10^m * p2 = ((10^m * p2) div 2^-e) * 2^-e + ((10^m * p2) mod 2^-e)
10416 // = ( d) * 2^-e + ( r)
10417 //
10418 // or
10419 // 10^m * p2 * 2^e = d + r * 2^e
10420 //
10421 // i.e.
10422 //
10423 // M+ = buffer + p2 * 2^e
10424 // = buffer + 10^-m * (d + r * 2^e)
10425 // = (buffer * 10^m + d) * 10^-m + 10^-m * r * 2^e
10426 //
10427 // and stop as soon as 10^-m * r * 2^e <= delta * 2^e
10428
10429 assert(p2 > delta);
10430
10431 int m = 0;
10432 for (;;)
10433 {
10434 // Invariant:
10435 // M+ = buffer * 10^-m + 10^-m * (d[-m-1] / 10 + d[-m-2] / 10^2 + ...) * 2^e
10436 // = buffer * 10^-m + 10^-m * (p2 ) * 2^e
10437 // = buffer * 10^-m + 10^-m * (1/10 * (10 * p2) ) * 2^e
10438 // = buffer * 10^-m + 10^-m * (1/10 * ((10*p2 div 2^-e) * 2^-e + (10*p2 mod 2^-e)) * 2^e
10439 //
10440 assert(p2 <= UINT64_MAX / 10);
10441 p2 *= 10;
10442 const uint64_t d = p2 >> -one.e; // d = (10 * p2) div 2^-e
10443 const uint64_t r = p2 & (one.f - 1); // r = (10 * p2) mod 2^-e
10444 //
10445 // M+ = buffer * 10^-m + 10^-m * (1/10 * (d * 2^-e + r) * 2^e
10446 // = buffer * 10^-m + 10^-m * (1/10 * (d + r * 2^e))
10447 // = (buffer * 10 + d) * 10^(-m-1) + 10^(-m-1) * r * 2^e
10448 //
10449 assert(d <= 9);
10450 buffer[length++] = static_cast<char>('0' + d); // buffer := buffer * 10 + d
10451 //
10452 // M+ = buffer * 10^(-m-1) + 10^(-m-1) * r * 2^e
10453 //
10454 p2 = r;
10455 m++;
10456 //
10457 // M+ = buffer * 10^-m + 10^-m * p2 * 2^e
10458 // Invariant restored.
10459
10460 // Check if enough digits have been generated.
10461 //
10462 // 10^-m * p2 * 2^e <= delta * 2^e
10463 // p2 * 2^e <= 10^m * delta * 2^e
10464 // p2 <= 10^m * delta
10465 delta *= 10;
10466 dist *= 10;
10467 if (p2 <= delta)
10468 {
10469 break;
10470 }
10471 }
10472
10473 // V = buffer * 10^-m, with M- <= V <= M+.
10474
10475 decimal_exponent -= m;
10476
10477 // 1 ulp in the decimal representation is now 10^-m.
10478 // Since delta and dist are now scaled by 10^m, we need to do the
10479 // same with ulp in order to keep the units in sync.
10480 //
10481 // 10^m * 10^-m = 1 = 2^-e * 2^e = ten_m * 2^e
10482 //
10483 const uint64_t ten_m = one.f;
10484 grisu2_round(buffer, length, dist, delta, p2, ten_m);
10485
10486 // By construction this algorithm generates the shortest possible decimal
10487 // number (Loitsch, Theorem 6.2) which rounds back to w.
10488 // For an input number of precision p, at least
10489 //
10490 // N = 1 + ceil(p * log_10(2))
10491 //
10492 // decimal digits are sufficient to identify all binary floating-point
10493 // numbers (Matula, "In-and-Out conversions").
10494 // This implies that the algorithm does not produce more than N decimal
10495 // digits.
10496 //
10497 // N = 17 for p = 53 (IEEE double precision)
10498 // N = 9 for p = 24 (IEEE single precision)
10499}
10500
10506inline void grisu2(char* buf, int& len, int& decimal_exponent,
10507 diyfp m_minus, diyfp v, diyfp m_plus)
10508{
10509 assert(m_plus.e == m_minus.e);
10510 assert(m_plus.e == v.e);
10511
10512 // --------(-----------------------+-----------------------)-------- (A)
10513 // m- v m+
10514 //
10515 // --------------------(-----------+-----------------------)-------- (B)
10516 // m- v m+
10517 //
10518 // First scale v (and m- and m+) such that the exponent is in the range
10519 // [alpha, gamma].
10520
10521 const cached_power cached = get_cached_power_for_binary_exponent(m_plus.e);
10522
10523 const diyfp c_minus_k(cached.f, cached.e); // = c ~= 10^-k
10524
10525 // The exponent of the products is = v.e + c_minus_k.e + q and is in the range [alpha,gamma]
10526 const diyfp w = diyfp::mul(v, c_minus_k);
10527 const diyfp w_minus = diyfp::mul(m_minus, c_minus_k);
10528 const diyfp w_plus = diyfp::mul(m_plus, c_minus_k);
10529
10530 // ----(---+---)---------------(---+---)---------------(---+---)----
10531 // w- w w+
10532 // = c*m- = c*v = c*m+
10533 //
10534 // diyfp::mul rounds its result and c_minus_k is approximated too. w, w- and
10535 // w+ are now off by a small amount.
10536 // In fact:
10537 //
10538 // w - v * 10^k < 1 ulp
10539 //
10540 // To account for this inaccuracy, add resp. subtract 1 ulp.
10541 //
10542 // --------+---[---------------(---+---)---------------]---+--------
10543 // w- M- w M+ w+
10544 //
10545 // Now any number in [M-, M+] (bounds included) will round to w when input,
10546 // regardless of how the input rounding algorithm breaks ties.
10547 //
10548 // And digit_gen generates the shortest possible such number in [M-, M+].
10549 // Note that this does not mean that Grisu2 always generates the shortest
10550 // possible number in the interval (m-, m+).
10551 const diyfp M_minus(w_minus.f + 1, w_minus.e);
10552 const diyfp M_plus (w_plus.f - 1, w_plus.e );
10553
10554 decimal_exponent = -cached.k; // = -(-k) = k
10555
10556 grisu2_digit_gen(buf, len, decimal_exponent, M_minus, w, M_plus);
10557}
10558
10564template <typename FloatType>
10565void grisu2(char* buf, int& len, int& decimal_exponent, FloatType value)
10566{
10567 static_assert(diyfp::kPrecision >= std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::digits + 3,
10568 "internal error: not enough precision");
10569
10570 assert(std::isfinite(value));
10571 assert(value > 0);
10572
10573 // If the neighbors (and boundaries) of 'value' are always computed for double-precision
10574 // numbers, all float's can be recovered using strtod (and strtof). However, the resulting
10575 // decimal representations are not exactly "short".
10576 //
10577 // The documentation for 'std::to_chars' (https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/to_chars)
10578 // says "value is converted to a string as if by std::sprintf in the default ("C") locale"
10579 // and since sprintf promotes float's to double's, I think this is exactly what 'std::to_chars'
10580 // does.
10581 // On the other hand, the documentation for 'std::to_chars' requires that "parsing the
10582 // representation using the corresponding std::from_chars function recovers value exactly". That
10583 // indicates that single precision floating-point numbers should be recovered using
10584 // 'std::strtof'.
10585 //
10586 // NB: If the neighbors are computed for single-precision numbers, there is a single float
10587 // (7.0385307e-26f) which can't be recovered using strtod. The resulting double precision
10588 // value is off by 1 ulp.
10589#if 0
10590 const boundaries w = compute_boundaries(static_cast<double>(value));
10591#else
10592 const boundaries w = compute_boundaries(value);
10593#endif
10594
10595 grisu2(buf, len, decimal_exponent, w.minus, w.w, w.plus);
10596}
10597
10603inline char* append_exponent(char* buf, int e)
10604{
10605 assert(e > -1000);
10606 assert(e < 1000);
10607
10608 if (e < 0)
10609 {
10610 e = -e;
10611 *buf++ = '-';
10612 }
10613 else
10614 {
10615 *buf++ = '+';
10616 }
10617
10618 auto k = static_cast<uint32_t>(e);
10619 if (k < 10)
10620 {
10621 // Always print at least two digits in the exponent.
10622 // This is for compatibility with printf("%g").
10623 *buf++ = '0';
10624 *buf++ = static_cast<char>('0' + k);
10625 }
10626 else if (k < 100)
10627 {
10628 *buf++ = static_cast<char>('0' + k / 10);
10629 k %= 10;
10630 *buf++ = static_cast<char>('0' + k);
10631 }
10632 else
10633 {
10634 *buf++ = static_cast<char>('0' + k / 100);
10635 k %= 100;
10636 *buf++ = static_cast<char>('0' + k / 10);
10637 k %= 10;
10638 *buf++ = static_cast<char>('0' + k);
10639 }
10640
10641 return buf;
10642}
10643
10653inline char* format_buffer(char* buf, int len, int decimal_exponent,
10654 int min_exp, int max_exp)
10655{
10656 assert(min_exp < 0);
10657 assert(max_exp > 0);
10658
10659 const int k = len;
10660 const int n = len + decimal_exponent;
10661
10662 // v = buf * 10^(n-k)
10663 // k is the length of the buffer (number of decimal digits)
10664 // n is the position of the decimal point relative to the start of the buffer.
10665
10666 if (k <= n and n <= max_exp)
10667 {
10668 // digits[000]
10669 // len <= max_exp + 2
10670
10671 std::memset(buf + k, '0', static_cast<size_t>(n - k));
10672 // Make it look like a floating-point number (#362, #378)
10673 buf[n + 0] = '.';
10674 buf[n + 1] = '0';
10675 return buf + (n + 2);
10676 }
10677
10678 if (0 < n and n <= max_exp)
10679 {
10680 // dig.its
10681 // len <= max_digits10 + 1
10682
10683 assert(k > n);
10684
10685 std::memmove(buf + (n + 1), buf + n, static_cast<size_t>(k - n));
10686 buf[n] = '.';
10687 return buf + (k + 1);
10688 }
10689
10690 if (min_exp < n and n <= 0)
10691 {
10692 // 0.[000]digits
10693 // len <= 2 + (-min_exp - 1) + max_digits10
10694
10695 std::memmove(buf + (2 + -n), buf, static_cast<size_t>(k));
10696 buf[0] = '0';
10697 buf[1] = '.';
10698 std::memset(buf + 2, '0', static_cast<size_t>(-n));
10699 return buf + (2 + (-n) + k);
10700 }
10701
10702 if (k == 1)
10703 {
10704 // dE+123
10705 // len <= 1 + 5
10706
10707 buf += 1;
10708 }
10709 else
10710 {
10711 // d.igitsE+123
10712 // len <= max_digits10 + 1 + 5
10713
10714 std::memmove(buf + 2, buf + 1, static_cast<size_t>(k - 1));
10715 buf[1] = '.';
10716 buf += 1 + k;
10717 }
10718
10719 *buf++ = 'e';
10720 return append_exponent(buf, n - 1);
10721}
10722
10723} // namespace dtoa_impl
10724
10735template <typename FloatType>
10736char* to_chars(char* first, const char* last, FloatType value)
10737{
10738 static_cast<void>(last); // maybe unused - fix warning
10739 assert(std::isfinite(value));
10740
10741 // Use signbit(value) instead of (value < 0) since signbit works for -0.
10742 if (std::signbit(value))
10743 {
10744 value = -value;
10745 *first++ = '-';
10746 }
10747
10748 if (value == 0) // +-0
10749 {
10750 *first++ = '0';
10751 // Make it look like a floating-point number (#362, #378)
10752 *first++ = '.';
10753 *first++ = '0';
10754 return first;
10755 }
10756
10757 assert(last - first >= std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::max_digits10);
10758
10759 // Compute v = buffer * 10^decimal_exponent.
10760 // The decimal digits are stored in the buffer, which needs to be interpreted
10761 // as an unsigned decimal integer.
10762 // len is the length of the buffer, i.e. the number of decimal digits.
10763 int len = 0;
10764 int decimal_exponent = 0;
10765 dtoa_impl::grisu2(first, len, decimal_exponent, value);
10766
10767 assert(len <= std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::max_digits10);
10768
10769 // Format the buffer like printf("%.*g", prec, value)
10770 constexpr int kMinExp = -4;
10771 // Use digits10 here to increase compatibility with version 2.
10772 constexpr int kMaxExp = std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::digits10;
10773
10774 assert(last - first >= kMaxExp + 2);
10775 assert(last - first >= 2 + (-kMinExp - 1) + std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::max_digits10);
10776 assert(last - first >= std::numeric_limits<FloatType>::max_digits10 + 6);
10777
10778 return dtoa_impl::format_buffer(first, len, decimal_exponent, kMinExp, kMaxExp);
10779}

10800// serialization //
10802
10804enum class error_handler_t
10805{
10806 strict,
10807 replace,
10808 ignore
10809};
